title: Extensionality over block indices for the equal-incidence-matrix isomorphism
intent: Reduce the claim that two ordered incidence systems with the same incidence matrix are isomorphic to the two obligations of the incidence_system_isomorphism locale, and discharge the block-multiset equality pointwise, one block index j at a time, rewriting each side through the block-representation lemmas.

parent.name: equal_inc_mat_isomorphism
parent.statement:
lemma equal_inc_mat_isomorphism: 
  assumes "D1.N = D2.N"
  shows "incidence_system_isomorphism D1.\<V> D1.\<B> D2.\<V> D2.\<B> (\<lambda> x . \<V>s' ! (List_Index.index \<V>s x))"

children.name: block_mat_cond_rev
children.statement:
lemma block_mat_cond_rev: 
  assumes "j < length \<B>s"
  shows "{i . i < length \<V>s \<and> N $$ (i, j) = 1} = ((List_Index.index) \<V>s) ` (\<B>s ! j)"
children.closed_by: intro Set.set_eqI iffI, then the two directions close by the project lemmas inc_matrix_point_in_block (line 1112) and inc_matrix_point_in_block_one (line 1122) of the same file
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: the reverse block-matrix condition: the set of point indices where column j of the incidence matrix is 1 equals the image of block j under the point-index function

children.name: block_mat_cond_rep'
children.statement: lemma block_mat_cond_rep': "j < length \<B>s \<Longrightarrow> (\<B>s ! j) = ((!) \<V>s) ` {i . i < length \<V>s \<and> N $$ (i, j) = 1}"
children.note: Analyst's paraphrase, replaced by the declaration's text: block j is the image, under point lookup (!) Vs, of the set of point indices where column j of the incidence matrix is 1

applicability.goal_shape: An equality of sets, lists or multisets of the form (image_mset f Bs = Bs') or (map f Bs = Bs'), proved by showing the two sides agree pointwise on each index j and lifting the pointwise equality to the whole object with nth_equalityI / mset_map.
applicability.use_when: Each side of the equality can be rewritten to the same common form by one named lemma (here both sides become the image of the index set {i. i < length Vs ∧ N $$ (i, j) = 1}), so the pointwise step closes by rewriting alone.
applicability.avoid_when: The two sides have different representations (a set comprehension on one side and an image on the other) with no single lemma bridging them; or the equality is not an image-of-common-index equality, so a case analysis or a different witness is needed.

consequences: The pointwise proof creates one obligation per block index j (the fix j subgoal inside the have "∧ j. ..."), plus the length-match obligation (len) that nth_equalityI needs, and finally the lift from list equality to multiset equality via mset_map. It relies on the index function List_Index.index being a bijection between the point set and {..<length Vs}, which needs the point list to be distinct (D1.distinct); with duplicate points the index step no longer inverts the block lookup.
